diagnostics.message: :resource.aws_s3_object.cloudformation_template: explicit depends_on of :resource.random_uuid.splunk_input_uuid is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`aws_s3_object.cloudformation_template` lists `random_uuid.splunk_input_uuid` in its `depends_on`, but both `key` and `source` already interpolate `random_uuid.splunk_input_uuid.result`, so the dependency is established implicitly and the explicit `depends_on` entry is redundant. (Its `depends_on` on `data.external.splunk_dm_version`, which produces the /tmp template file, is not redundant.)

`null_resource.create_integration` runs `scripts/create_splunk_integration.sh`, which deploys the Splunk integration CloudFormation stack from the template URL built out of `var.cloudformation_s3_config` + the uuid (see `local.template_url`) — i.e. it requires `aws_s3_object.cloudformation_template` to already be uploaded to S3. Nothing in `create_integration` (triggers or local-exec) references that object, so Terraform may run the local-exec provisioning before the template exists, causing the stack creation to fail. Add an ordering dependency on `aws_s3_object.cloudformation_template`, preferably by folding its hash into `triggers` so the integration is also recreated when the template changes.
